builds.name: Reference: Ranked top core
builds.goal: Reference for Riven: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ top players use most (2,581 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 60.2% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A melee combo fighter who interleaves charged attacks with dashes and control. AD improves spell damage, passive attacks and her shield, so coherent sequencing is valuable. The current top provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Axiom Arc → Endless Hunger → Death's Dance. Conqueror keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Ionian Boots of Lucidity, Maw of Malmortius, Guardian Angel.
builds.summary: The proven top baseline: Axiom Arc → Endless Hunger → Death's Dance, with Conqueror.
testPlan: Play it in top as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Axiom Arc → Endless Hunger → Death's Dance) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 60.2% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Axiom Arc → Endless Hunger → Death's Dance.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula:
Riven dashes forward, dealing [45 / 75 / 105 / 135 / 165 + (0.6 / 0.65 / 0.7 / 0.75 / 0.8) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage. She can Recast this Ability twice. The first Recast is the same as the original, but the second has a different effect:

Recast: Riven leaps forward and slams, dealing [45 / 75 / 105 / 135 / 165 + (0.6 / 0.65 / 0.7 / 0.75 / 0.8) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and Knocks Up nearby enemies for 0.75 seconds.
Riven's sword emits a burst of runic energy, dealing [65 / 95 / 125 / 155 / 185 + (1) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and Stunning for [0.75] seconds.
Riven quickly dashes and gains [70 / 95 / 120 / 145 / 170 + (1.1) × AD[statFormula=2]] Shield for 1.5 seconds.
Using an Ability grants Riven a charge for 6 seconds (max [3]). Her Attacks spend a charge to deal an additional [(characterLevelInterpolation(0.3 → 0.45; raw flags preserved)) × AD] physical damage.

Riven's weapon surges with spiritual energy, granting her [(0.2) × AD] Attack Damage and increased range on damaging Abilities and Attacks for [15] seconds. While active, she can Recast.

Recast: Riven fires a wind slash that deals between [100 / 150 / 200 + (0.55) × AD[statFormula=2]] and [300 / 450 / 600 + (1.65) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage, based on their missing Health.

builds.name: Runic Blade crit weave
builds.summary: Test runic blade crit weave against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test runic blade crit weave against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Runic Blade charges are spent on real attacks and R boosts total AD for fifteen seconds; Essence Reaver adds a separate physical Spellblade packet after a cast. Crit strengthens ordinary attacks, while Shojin preserves basic spell access; Q remains a physical spell rather than a crit attack.
testPlan: Required state: Spend charges between Q recasts instead of dumping all spells first.
Compare three charge attacks plus Q against Q-only burst.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Attack exposure and low durability lose the normal mobile trade.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Crit does not multiply Broken Wings or the whole Runic Blade packet without a classification test.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Essence Reaver, Infinity Edge, Bloodthirster, Spear of Shojin, Death's Dance, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Physical matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Riven: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A melee combo fighter who interleaves charged attacks with dashes and control. AD improves spell damage, passive attacks and her shield, so coherent sequencing is valuable. Measure real attack weaving, Q casts and AD-backed shields. Crit only applies where permitted; poor animation/cancel timing can erase a theoretical attack advantage. Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
builds.summary: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Riven: Measure real attack weaving, Q casts and AD-backed shields. Crit only applies where permitted; poor animation/cancel timing can erase a theoretical attack advantage.

Start with the early core (Stridebreaker, then matchup armor) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: None. Do not treat mana regeneration as None recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Riven lashes out in a series of strikes. This ability can be reactivated three times in a short time frame with the third hit knocking back nearby enemies. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.

The route fails Riven's stated kit question: Measure real attack weaving, Q casts and AD-backed shields. Crit only applies where permitted; poor animation/cancel timing can erase a theoretical attack advantage.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.
Full cost 16,100 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Stridebreaker, then matchup armor. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Randuin's Omen, Spirit Visage, Sterak's Gage are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Resource: None. Do not treat mana regeneration as None recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Bloodmail shield endurance
builds.summary: Test bloodmail shield endurance against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test bloodmail shield endurance against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Valor's shield has a 1.1 AD[source modifier] term; Bloodmail supplies AD from item health, while Visage increases received shields and Sundered Sky rewards an attack between Q recasts. R's AD amplification can improve both offensive spells and shield potential within its fifteen seconds.
testPlan: Required state: Repeatedly use E before retaliation and spend passive charges.
Record E shield and damage at identical missing health before and during R.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Healing reduction and burst arriving after the 1.5-second shield defeat the sustain.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Health does not directly scale Valor; the proposed link is Bloodmail's AD conversion.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Overlord's Bloodmail, Sundered Sky, Spear of Shojin, Spirit Visage, Sterak's Gage, Plated Steelcaps. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
